primary_source.citation: Riihimäki M, Hemminki A, Sundquist J, Hemminki K. Patterns of metastasis in colon and rectal cancer. Scientific Reports. 2016;6:29765.
primary_source.study_type: Population-based registry study; Swedish Cancer Registry linked with National Patient Register and Cause of Death Register; n=31,285 colon cancer patients

MUSCULOSKELETAL.frequency_pct_range: low overall; up to 10% as single met in stage I disease

biomarkers.name: KRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: RAS-mutant tumours DO NOT respond to anti-EGFR (cetuximab, panitumumab). KRAS G12C (~3-4% of mCRC; ~1-3% of all CRC): adagrasib + cetuximab is an established targeted option; sotorasib + panitumumab has supportive trial data. Non-G12C: currently no approved direct targeted therapy

biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E
biomarkers.clinical_use: Strong adverse prognostic. Previously treated metastatic disease: encorafenib + cetuximab (BEACON CRC). Often co-occurs with MSI-H, right-sided, older women. Enriched in right-sided disease

biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR
biomarkers.clinical_use: Universal screening for Lynch syndrome workup (germline testing if MLH1/PMS2 loss is not explained by MLH1 promoter hypermethylation/BRAF V600E). Stage II: better prognosis, limited/no benefit from adjuvant fluoropyrimidine-only therapy. Metastatic: pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-177) or nivolumab ± ipilimumab first-line — often dramatic and durable responses

biomarkers.name: HER2 (ERBB2) amplification
biomarkers.clinical_use: Trastuzumab + pertuzumab (HERACLES, MyPathway); tucatinib + trastuzumab (MOUNTAINEER); trastuzumab deruxtecan / T-DXd (DESTINY-CRC01/02). Also predicts reduced anti-EGFR benefit

biomarkers.name: POLE / POLD1 exonuclease-domain mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Ultra-high TMB with excellent IO response despite often MSS status; can present as 'Lynch-like' clinically

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.prevalence: Usually low in MSS; high in MSI-H and POLE/POLD1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Tissue-agnostic pembrolizumab if TMB ≥10 mut/Mb, although in colorectal cancer benefit is largely confined to MSI-H/dMMR or POLE/POLD1-ultramutated tumours

biomarkers.name: Tumor sidedness (right vs left)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Right-sided (caecum through transverse): worse prognosis, more BRAF/MSI/mucinous, reduced anti-EGFR benefit even in RAS-wildtype. Left-sided (splenic flexure through rectum): anti-EGFR preferred in RAS-wildtype

biomarkers.name: CEA
biomarkers.clinical_use: Elevated in many CRC patients; standard for post-operative surveillance and response monitoring; baseline value prognostic

biomarkers.name: CA 19-9
biomarkers.clinical_use: Complementary to CEA; more useful in mucinous / peritoneal disease

biomarkers.name: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) — Signatera, Guardant Reveal
biomarkers.clinical_use: MRD detection post-resection; stage II ctDNA-positive identifies high recurrence risk and can guide adjuvant chemotherapy decisions (DYNAMIC trial). Surveillance is often more sensitive than CEA. Increasing role in adjuvant decisions

biomarkers.name: Consensus Molecular Subtypes (CMS1-4)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Research use primarily; CMS4 has worst prognosis; may guide future trial stratification

biomarkers.name: APC
biomarkers.clinical_use: Foundational WNT-pathway driver and hallmark alteration in the conventional adenoma-carcinoma sequence; important biologically but not currently a routine predictive biomarker for approved targeted therapy

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common late driver in chromosomal-instability pathway; prognostic associations are context-dependent and it is not currently used as a standard predictive biomarker

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Glandular adenocarcinoma with variable mucin content and desmoplastic reaction
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Well / moderately / poorly differentiated; MSI-H tumours often 'poorly differentiated' by morphology but behave better than expected

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Sharply divided by CMS subtype — CMS1 (MSI, hypermutated) is highly inflamed; CMS4 (mesenchymal) is TGF-β driven and immune-excluded
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: CMS4 tumours have desmoplastic fibroblast-rich stroma; MSI-H tumours often have Crohn-like lymphocytic reaction

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Intestinal stem cells at crypt base (LGR5+ stem cells) or transit-amplifying progenitors
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Endoderm — midgut (proximal colon to splenic flexure) and hindgut (distal colon, rectum) derivatives
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Well-to-moderately differentiated intestinal-type glandular differentiation (CDX2+/CK20+, MUC2+); consensus molecular subtypes (CMS) reflect distinct lineage-related biology
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Right-sided arises from serrated pathway (BRAF-driven with CIMP methylator phenotype) or MSI pathway; left-sided arises from conventional adenoma-carcinoma sequence (APC → KRAS → TP53); embryologic midgut/hindgut boundary contributes to biological differences
